links.outcome: AUROC drop when applying MIMIC-IV-trained sepsis model to German ICU data
links.effect: Continuous evaluation, 6-hour horizon: AUROC 0.67 (95% CI 0.66-0.68) on BerlinICU versus 0.84 (95% CI 0.83-0.85) on MIMIC-IV test set.
links.quote: Application of a temporal convolutional network model to BerlinICU yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.67 (95% CI 0.66-0.68) for continuous evaluation with a 6-hour prediction horizon, compared with 0.84 (95% CI 0.83-0.85) on the test set of Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV.

links.outcome: Variation in AUROC across evaluation strategies for the same model and dataset
links.effect: Fixed horizon AUROC 0.61 (95% CI 0.60-0.62) versus about 0.67 for continuous and peak score evaluation; metrics improved with shorter horizons.
links.quote: The same model applied to the same dataset yields markedly different performance metrics depending on the evaluation approach.

unlisted_practices: Choice of evaluation strategy (fixed horizon vs peak score vs continuous) and onset/length-of-stay matching for sepsis prediction metrics

screen.reason: Evaluates how different model validation/evaluation strategies (continuous vs fixed horizon vs peak score) impact performance metrics and real-world clinical interpretability of sepsis risk prediction models on a multisite dataset.
